description: Turn an old Android phone into a customizable desk panel and touch control deck for Windows, Linux and macOS. 124 widgets and 30 templates for system stats, AI coding, media and automation, in 13 languages. USB or paired Wi-Fi. No cloud required.

latest_release.name: PhoneBox 0.9.24
latest_release.body:
A security fix for phones connected over USB: the USB connection now answers only the PhoneBox app, so **update the
agent and the phone app together**. Also: audio mixers show one control per app on Windows, Microphone and Output
selection fit side by side, device batteries refresh faster, and a phone that is plugged in can be left as it is.

**Security**
- The USB connection answers only the PhoneBox app. `adb reverse` now ends on a loopback port of its own instead of the
  agent's local port, over TLS that the app pins to the agent's certificate, and every request must carry a key the
  app makes. The agent reads that key and hands over the certificate's fingerprint over adb, through a place only the
  adb shell can reach, after checking that it belongs to the PhoneBox app. Over USB the phone reaches the same paths as
  over Wi-Fi, plus its pairing data and the feed proxy; the settings, shortcut tests and pairing controls stay on the
  computer. **Update the agent and the phone app together**: an older app can't use USB with this agent, and the
  settings page offers its update. If an app you don't trust was ever on the panel phone, pair Wi-Fi again and make a
  new webhook key, and renew the Home Assistant, Discord and other tokens in the settings
  ([GHSA-j6qc-pm3p-fhg7](https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/security/advisories/GHSA-j6qc-pm3p-fhg7)).

**Widgets**
- Audio mixers on Windows: one control per app instead of one per Windows audio session. An app that plays on two
  outputs, or that you moved to another output, no longer shows up twice. Apps get the name Windows' own mixer shows
  (MSI Center, not `DCv2`), and the phone lists only apps that are playing, plus System sounds. Volume and mute reach
  every session of the app; ducking, the sleep timer and audio profiles still see every session (#292,
  [RawreeUX](https://github.com/RawreeUX)).
- Microphone and Output selection: a **Layout** option (horizontal, grid or the vertical list as before), so several
  devices fit side by side on a phone, and **Device labels** to show a short name or an emoji for a device
  (`Speakers (USB Audio CODEC) = 🔊`, one per line, matched by its exact name). Switching still uses the device itself,
  and the full name stays in the button's tooltip (#294, [RawreeUX](https://github.com/RawreeUX)).
- Audio mixers: mute is a compact speaker icon under the volume instead of a wide Mute / Unmute button, so many apps
  fit without overlapping (#293, [RawreeUX](https://github.com/RawreeUX)).
- Device batteries on Windows: a paired Bluetooth device that has disconnected (a controller or headset turned off) is
  no longer shown with its last battery reading (#295, [RawreeUX](https://github.com/RawreeUX)).
- Device batteries: the Razer Barracuda Pro, read through its 2.4 GHz receiver, also while Razer Synapse runs (#296,
  [RawreeUX](https://github.com/RawreeUX)).
- Device batteries refresh every 20 seconds while the widget is shown, instead of once a minute; macOS stays at once a
  minute, because reading headphones there takes seconds (#297, [RawreeUX](https://github.com/RawreeUX)).

**Agent**
- A new **Settings › Display › Open PhoneBox when the phone is plugged in** option (on by default, so nothing
  changes until you turn it off). Off, a phone that connects over USB, or reconnects after adb restarts, is left as it
  is instead of being woken with the panel brought to the front, for a phone that also runs app tests over adb (#291,
  [snackncode](https://github.com/snackncode)).

detail.readme:
PhoneBox

English · Türkçe · Deutsch · Français · Español · Italiano · Português · Nederlands · Polski · Русский · Ελληνικά · Tiếng Việt · 中文 (简体)

Turn an old Android phone into a desk panel for your computer.
PC stats, AI coding sessions, music and touch controls over USB or Wi-Fi.
Windows, Linux and macOS. No root, PhoneBox account or cloud service required.

Try the live demo · Download · Quick start


Example layouts with demo data.

PhoneBox pairs a full-screen **Android app** with a small **desktop agent**. Build your panel in a browser-based visual editor: **126 widgets**, **30 templates**, multiple pages and a live preview. Connect several phones with their own layouts, or switch one phone between paired computers. ## What you can do | Use it for | What appears on the phone | |---|---| | **PC monitoring** | CPU, GPU, RAM, disks, network and ping; charts, GPU details and process controls | | **AI coding** | Claude, Codex and Antigravity quotas, reset times and burn-rate forecasts; local Claude Code and Codex sessions; GitHub reviews and CI status | | **Touch controls** | App and URL shortcuts, key combinations and macros; application audio, microphone, media, OBS and system controls through [Control Deck](docs/CONTROL-DECK.md) | | **Everyday use** | Now Playing, internet radio, clocks, weather, calendars, notes, checklists, pomodoro and timers | | **Automation** | Webhook values and notifications, Home Assistant controls and rules that react to activity on the computer | Tap an AI session for its model, timing and token details. Opt in to Codex or Claude Code permission prompts to answer **Allow** or **Deny** from the phone. Optional [CodexBar integration](docs/GUIDE.md#widgets) adds quota providers and a cost overview.


A tour with demo data: notifications, permission prompts and automatic page switching. Watch the MP4

## Quick start You need an **Android 5+ phone** (Android 6 or later recommended) and a supported computer. USB uses a data cable and USB debugging; Wi-Fi pairing works without either. Release agents include .NET, so you do not need to install the runtime. ### 1. Install the desktop agent **Windows 10/11 x64** — paste into a normal PowerShell window: ```powershell irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/main/setup.ps1 | iex ``` **Linux or macOS** — run as your own user: ```sh curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/main/setup.sh | bash ``` Setup downloads the latest release, checks its SHA-256 checksum, offers missing dependencies and start-at-login, and opens the settings at . It can also install the Android app over USB. Run setup again to update or repair the installation while keeping settings and pairings. > **Windows signing:** release agents are currently unsigned while the SignPath Foundation application is pending. > SmartScreen or antivirus software may warn or block them. See the [code signing policy](#code-signing-policy) > and [installation warnings](docs/SETUP.md#quick-start). USB debugging should be authorized only on computers you trust. Read the scripts before running them: [Windows](setup.ps1) · [Linux/macOS](setup.sh). The [installation guide](docs/SETUP.md) covers options, dependencies, install paths, troubleshooting and uninstalling. ### 2. Connect the phone | USB | Wi-Fi only | |---|---| | Enable **Developer options → USB debugging**, connect a data cable and accept the phone's authorization prompt. Let setup install the app, or use **Settings → General → Install the phone app**. | Install the APK from the [latest release](https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/releases/latest). Wi-Fi is off by default: open the settings page (tray icon, or `http://127.0.0.1:8765`), turn on **General → Wi-Fi & Tailscale → Let the phone connect without the USB cable**, click **Save**, then **Restart to apply** at the top. Choose **Pair a phone over Wi-Fi**, scan the pairing QR code and confirm the matching check code. | | Wakes and opens the panel on connection; supports app updates over adb. | No adb or developer options needed; install app updates manually unless you later configure USB. | The phone app is not in any app store; it comes only from this repository's releases. It runs on Android 5.0 and newer; there is no iOS version. For automatic USB/Wi-Fi fallback, enable Wi-Fi and connect the phone over USB once. [Connection details and Tailscale setup →](docs/SETUP.md#wi-fi--tailscale) ### 3. Make it yours Open (or double-click the Windows tray icon). Under **Pages**, choose a template, drag and resize widgets, then **Save**. Use **Live preview** to see unsaved edits with live data. Swipe, tap the page dots or use the phone's volume keys to move between pages.
Other installation methods - **Manual download:** unzip the agent for your system from the [release page](https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/releases/latest) and run it. Install the APK on the phone. Checksums and build provenance accompany the release assets. - **Scoop (Windows):** ```powershell scoop bucket add phonebox https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox scoop install main/adb phonebox/phonebox ``` - **From source:** see the [installation guide](docs/SETUP.md#other-ways-to-install) and [development guide](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). - **winget:** manifests are prepared in [packaging/winget](packaging/winget); see the installation guide for details.
## Pages & templates Start with Home, System, AI quotas, Sessions, Music, Planner, Automation or a Control Deck template, then adapt the 12 × 6 grid to your phone. Portrait and landscape layouts are supported. Smart Stack puts up to 12 widgets in one slot. | Home | AI sessions | |---|---| | ![Clock, weather, media and PC metrics](docs/screenshots/home.png) | ![Coding sessions and GitHub activity](docs/screenshots/work.png) | | **System** | **Layout editor** | | ![CPU, GPU, memory and network charts](docs/screenshots/system.png) | ![Pages and widget settings in the visual editor](docs/screenshots/settings-editor.png) | Screenshots use demo data. [Browse the template gallery and widgets](docs/GUIDE.md#pages--templates). Change fonts, size, spacing, corners and surfaces globally or for one page or widget with the [appearance guide](docs/APPEARANCE.md). ## Platform support | | Windows | Linux | macOS | |---|---|---|---| | Release builds | x64 | x64 / ARM64, glibc | Apple silicon / Intel | | CPU, RAM, disks, network, processes | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | GPU data | Windows counters; NVIDIA via `nvidia-smi`; extra sensors via [LibreHardwareMonitor](docs/SETUP.md#librehardwaremonitor-on-windows) | NVIDIA / AMD; Intel clock | Apple silicon, when exposed by macOS | | Media | System media sessions | `playerctl` | `nowplaying-cli`; Spotify / Music fallback | | Volume | Native | `wpctl` / `pactl` | System output; availability varies by device | | Agent interface | Tray icon + browser settings | Browser settings | Browser settings | Widgets depend on the host's hardware, installed tools and permissions. Advanced Control Deck features have [their own platform requirements](docs/CONTROL-DECK.md). Windows ARM and musl Linux (such as Alpine) do not have release builds. See the [full compatibility table](docs/SETUP.md#what-works-where). ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [Installation and connections](docs/SETUP.md) | Setup options, warnings, manual and source installs, USB, Wi-Fi, Tailscale, updates, uninstall and troubleshooting | | [User guide](docs/GUIDE.md) | Template gallery, widgets, AI integrations, editor, Claude Code prompts, webhooks and automation rules | | [Appearance](docs/APPEARANCE.md) | Fonts, surfaces, presets, inheritance and live preview | | [Control Deck](docs/CONTROL-DECK.md) | Audio, media, OBS, shortcuts, tasks, protocols, dependencies and platform limits | | [Discord widget](docs/DISCORD.md) | Creating the Discord application, connecting it, controls and troubleshooting | | [Development](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md) | Architecture, local demo, builds, tests, widget sources and isolated agent runs | | [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Contribution scope, review expectations, privacy and required checks | | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Release history and unreleased changes | | [Release checklist](docs/RELEASING.md) | Maintainer build, signing and publication workflow | The [UMIDIGI BISON extras](extras/umidigi-bison) contain the reversible, no-root tune-up used on the original development phone. ## Security & privacy The desktop settings server listens on `127.0.0.1:8765`. USB reaches the agent through `adb reverse` on a loopback port of its own, over TLS pinned like Wi-Fi, with a key the phone app makes and the agent reads over adb. Optional Wi-Fi uses HTTPS on port 8766 with a pinned certificate and a paired key. Settings and pairing endpoints stay local. The phone requests configured actions by ID; commands and integration credentials stay on the computer. PhoneBox has no telemetry, analytics or accounts of its own. Optional widgets and integrations contact external services for weather, quotas, GitHub and other data, and the agent checks GitHub for updates. Supported public feeds can fall back through the agent over USB when the phone has no internet. The [privacy policy](PRIVACY.md) lists outbound connections and how to disable them. Read the [security details](docs/GUIDE.md#security--privacy). To report a vulnerability, follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Development The agent uses **.NET 10**; the Android app uses **Kotlin and a WebView** with plain JavaScript widgets. For Android builds, install **JDK 17** and **Android SDK Platform 35** (the SDK the app is built with; the app itself runs on Android 5.0, API 21, and later). Preview the panel and editor from source with Python 3, using simulated data: ```sh python tools/demo-server.py ``` Open or . See [development commands](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md#development) for running the agent, building the APK and testing changes. Contributions are welcome; start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Code signing policy Free code signing provided by [SignPath.io](https://about.signpath.io/), certificate by [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org/). - **Windows agent:** the SignPath Foundation application is pending; releases are unsigned until approved. The intended signing target is `PhoneBoxAgent.exe` in the `win-x64` release zip, built by the [release workflow](.github/workflows/release.yml). Every signing request requires manual approval. Bundled runtime and library notices are in [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt](agent/PhoneBox.Agent/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt). - **Android app:** release APKs use the project's own signing key, independently of SignPath. - **Team roles:** committer, reviewer and signing approver: [ersinkoc](https://github.com/ersinkoc). Pull requests from other contributors are reviewed before merging. - **Privacy:** see the [privacy policy](PRIVACY.md). ## Thanks People who tested PhoneBox on their own hardware: - [anandyakshit](https://github.com/anandyakshit): Android 7 support, on an Android 7.1.1 phone ([#73](https://github.com/ersinkoc/phonebox/issues/73)). ## Sponsor
